subAgents: none spawned. The dispatch forbids it; all work and all verification was done by this agent.
missionPremise: vendor/sc-kit.css declares --sc-font-ui as Inter and --sc-font-data as IBM Plex Mono; the package shipped neither family and no @font-face, so every design built from it rendered in a system fallback and the eight-step type ramp was lost with nothing saying so. The product escapes this because smartcity-dashboards/web/index.html loads both from a font host. Authorised by _decisions/2026-08-18_smartcity_kit_component_package.md gate item 4 as amended 2026-08-18: the package may ship @font-face rules, and only those, for families the canonical token block already names.
completionPredicate: A consumer installing the built package and importing what the README names renders in Inter and IBM Plex Mono, provable by a browser rather than by reading CSS; and the granted exception cannot widen, because a test fails on any rule that is not an @font-face, any family no font token names, any src url that does not resolve to a shipped file, and any shipped file that does not match its pinned hash, with each of those watched failing against a real injected violation.
scopeBasis: Bounded by the amendment. Fonts only, @font-face only, families the token block already names. dist/kit.css byte equality is untouched because it is load-bearing, so the faces ship as a separate export rather than folded in. No component, class, or styling rule was added; vendor/sc-kit.css and vendor/shell.css were not edited; smartcity-dashboards was not touched; nothing was published to npm; no repo LICENSE file was added, that being held for an operator ruling, while the fonts' own OFL texts are included because the licence requires it.

pathsNotExercisedByAnyTest.path: bundler rewriting of url("./fonts/*.woff2") in dist/fonts.css
pathsNotExercisedByAnyTest.why: THIS IS THE LARGEST LOCAL-VERSUS-CONSUMER DIVERGENCE. Locally and in CI the sheet is served over plain http, where the relative url resolves against the stylesheet's own URL and always works. A consumer imports it through Vite, webpack, Next or Rollup, each of which parses url() and rewrites it to a hashed asset path. None of that is exercised anywhere. A bundler configured not to emit font assets would produce 404s that every check here still passes.

pathsNotExercisedByAnyTest.path: an installed tarball actually rendering with fonts
pathsNotExercisedByAnyTest.why: prove-fonts runs against dist/, not against an extracted tarball. The tarball is covered by static assertions only: every url() in the packed fonts.css must match a tarball entry, and the licence texts must be inside it. End-to-end 'installed package renders in Inter' is proven by composition, not observed.

no test runs it and CI never invokes it, deliberately: it reaches the network, and a build that reaches the network is not reproducible. If the font host changes its response shape the failure appears only on the next hand-run. Its output is what the gate checks, so a bad fetch cannot ship silently, but a broken fetcher is discovered late.

only the 7 latin slices are ever parsed by a browser, because the probe text is Latin. The other 36 are checked for existence and hash but never rendered. A file that hashes correctly and is unrenderable would pass. Counting rule: 7 of 43 loaded, denominator is every registered face file.
woff2 and unicode-range behaviour in Firefox and Safari is not exercised. Chrome is the only engine any check here runs.
asserted as a declaration string in every rule; the swap period itself is never observed.

pathsNotExercisedByAnyTest.path: the mono width comparison on a host whose default monospace has a 0.600em advance
pathsNotExercisedByAnyTest.why: on Linux CI the mono margin is 10.88px, against 74.53px on Windows, because the Linux fallback is a 0.602em face. On a host whose default monospace advance equalled IBM Plex Mono's exactly, that particular assertion would be vacuous. It is not the only signal: the FontFaceSet assertion is independent of metrics and still fires.
